lesson_title: One Message, a Chain of Forwards: Geometric Sequences
hook_text: A message reaches 2 people. Each forwards it to 3 more. By round ten it reaches a small town. Here's the formula behind it.
clip_script: A message goes to 2 people. Each of them forwards it to 3 more. Round one: 2 people. Round two: 6. Round three: 18. Adding? No — multiplying. That's a geometric sequence, and its engine is one formula: start, times ratio to the power of the jumps. Round ten is 2 times 3 to the NINTH — nine, not ten, because round one is the start, not a forward. Three to the ninth is 19 683. Times two: 39 366 people. From two phones to a small town in nine forwards — addition climbs, multiplication explodes. And the formula runs backwards too. Which round hits exactly 1458 people? Two times 3 to the n minus one equals 1458. Divide by two: 729. Count your threes: 729 is 3 to the sixth. So n minus one is six — round seven. Same-base exponents, straight from the algebra you already own. The whole topic is one sentence: start times ratio to the jumps. That sentence prices compound interest, inflation, and every viral chain on your phone.
visual_style: Phone screens lighting up in a spreading tree over a township map at night, each round tripling the glow, a counter racing from 2 to 39 366; the tree rewinding to find round seven.
mood: Electric, escalating, a snap of awe at the explosion.
pacing: Quick triples through the early rounds, a breath before three to the ninth lands, decisive on the reverse question.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and command the mathematics that runs interest, inflation and every viral chain.
